subjects.en: Dr. Charles C.L. Kao / Chaolong Kao
facts: Born 1932
Graduated from Tainan Theological College and Seminary (TTCS)
Recognized by President Shoki Coe and sent to study in the United States
Earned a master's degree in the United States
Returned to teach at TTCS
In 1965, during the centenary celebration of the Taiwanese church, returned to the U.S. to attend Harvard Divinity School for doctoral degree
After obtaining his doctorate, remained at Harvard to conduct academic research
Former Assistant Professor at Tainan Theological College and Seminary (TTCS), Formosa
Before accepting the call, was a Visiting Scholar at Harvard University
Was called in September 1971 by the Presbytery of Los Angeles Southwest as the organizing minister of the Formosan Presbyterian Church in Los Angeles
Was the only Taiwanese pastor in the U.S. at that time with a doctoral degree
Met all requirements regarding age, degree, and experience for the organizing pastor role
After due diligence and discussions through the Presbytery, all procedures were completed
In place by September 1971, assuming the role of organizing pastor
Officially represented the United Presbyterian Church and led the Taiwanese congregation toward becoming a formal member of the United Presbyterian Church
Preached in his mother tongue (Taiwanese) on the first Sunday following the founding of the church
Delivered a sermon titled 'The Blessed Land'
His faithful, humble, and quiet service reflects the words of Jesus: 'Well done, good and faithful servant'
Albert Lai was familiar with him as a student from TTCS
Pastor Kao flew to San Francisco Theological Seminary to attend Albert Lai's graduation ceremony in May 1972
Officiated at Albert Lai's wedding at the Formosan Presbyterian Church in Los Angeles in July 1972
This was the first wedding held after the establishment of the Los Angeles Presbyterian Church

quotes.text: Rev. Dr. Charles C.L. Kao was called in September 1971 by the Presbytery of Los Angeles Southwest in behalf of Formosan congregation as the organizing minister.

Dr. Kao, former Assistant Professor at Tainan Theological College, Formosa, is also a native Formosan. Before he accepted this new position, he was a Visiting Scholar at Harvard University, Massachusetts.

On the very first Sunday following the founding of the first Taiwanese church in Los Angeles, Brother Albert Lai preached in his mother tongue (Taiwanese), delivering a sermon titled 'The Blessed Land.'

I returned to San Francisco Theological Seminary to finish my doctoral dissertation. In May 1972, I completed my doctoral degree, and Pastor Kao specially took the time to fly to San Francisco Theological Seminary to attend my graduation ceremony.

In July of the same year, my fiancée, Jane Hatsuko Ueno... and I held our wedding ceremony at the Formosan Presbyterian Church in Los Angeles, officiated by Pastor Kao. This was the first wedding held after the establishment of the Los Angeles Presbyterian Church.

facts: Graduated from Tainan Theological College and Seminary (TTCS)
Came to the United States in the early 1960s
Entered San Francisco Theological Seminary
After obtaining his master's degree, worked in a Japanese church
In 1967, switched to the United Methodist Church
Was assigned to a Japanese church in Fresno, Central California
Fresno is over two hundred miles from Los Angeles, about a three to four-hour drive
Was the pastor of the Fresno Japanese church
Was aware of the Formosan community in Los Angeles
Knew there were many Taiwanese people in Los Angeles, including students and their families
Noted that there were many Taiwanese children of the Presbyterian Church in Taiwan who longed for a Taiwanese church
Got to know several church friends through Professor Isiah Lee
Desired to establish a Taiwanese church in Los Angeles
Had just been accepted into the United Methodist Church and was serving as a pastor in English and Japanese
Was still adjusting to the management of the denomination
Was serving as a pastor in English and Japanese for the first time in a mainstream American church
Had a wife and small children and needed a reliable source of income
Could not leave his current position to start a Taiwanese church in Los Angeles
Decided to use one month of leave he was entitled to as a pastor in the United Methodist Church
Conducted a short-term experiment in August 1970
Held services and meals in Taiwanese
Invited the large Taiwanese population in Los Angeles to participate
The primary goal was to test the feasibility of establishing a Taiwanese church in Los Angeles
Consulted with the pastor of Century United Methodist Church in Los Angeles
Borrowed the church's facilities for a month
The Century Church was a Japanese church under the United Methodist Church
Located at the intersection of Normandie Ave and 35th Street, not far from USC
The middle-aged Japanese pastor agreed to provide full support without charging a penny
The pastor was also Taiwanese, born in Japan, named Peter Chen
Every Sunday afternoon, Pastor Peter Chen stayed at the church after the Japanese congregation met in the morning
The experimental church was consecrated 'Taiyou Church' (台友教會, Taiwanese Friendly Church)
First experimental Sunday worship: August 9, 1970 — 22 adults and 11 children attended
The four-week experimental church was conducted vibrantly and smoothly
After four weeks, Jonah Chang's one-month leave came to an end
He had to return to Fresno to continue his normal work
The experimental church had to come to an end on August 30
After Rev. Chang led the worship service, he asked everyone to stay for a discussion
The majority of the congregation envisioned the importance of carrying on such a fellowship
Decided to organize a church despite having no pastor or outside financial support
The church would be officially established and named 'Formosan Presbyterian Church in Los Angeles' on September 6
The work of establishing a Taiwanese church that Rev. Chang initiated was temporarily handed over to Albert Lai

quotes.text: In August 1970, Reverend Jonah Chang of the United Methodist Church in Fresno, California, a former minister of Presbyterian Church of Formosa, started a one-month experimental church to test the feasibility of such a church group in the Formosan community.
On the first experimental Sunday worship held on August 9, 1970, by Rev. Jonah Chang, 22 adults and 11 children attended.
Rev. Jonah Chang noted this situation and got to know several church friends, desiring to establish a Taiwanese church in Los Angeles.

After Rev. Chang led the worship service, he asked everyone to stay for a discussion... the majority of the congregation envisioned the importance of carrying on such fellowship among the Formosan people and decided to organize a church.

facts: Was a student of Dr. Barclay at Tainan Theological College and Seminary (TTCS)
Attended TTCS from 1932 to 1936
In the academic year of 1935-1936 (his final year at TTCS), was elected as the president of the student council
That year, Dr. Barclay passed away on October 5, 1935, at the Sin-lâu Hospital
At the funeral, his father and his classmates represented the student council and carried the coffin to be buried in the Christian cemetery
Preached in every corner of Taiwan
Traveled to many countries around the world to spread the Gospel
Served at churches in Huwei, Chingliao, Wu-niu-lan (now the Ailan Church), and Beigang
Built the Beigang Church
Pursued further studies at Nanking Theological Seminary
Served as an evangelist for the 'Centennial Doubling Campaign'
Assisted in the establishment of churches in the United States
Founded the United Bible Societies work in Taiwan from Beigang
Moved from Beigang Church to Taichung, where they officially established an office, a warehouse, and hired staff
The United Bible Societies began with him alone during its founding period while he was still serving at Beigang Church
Coordinated the selection of talents from various Christian denominations to collaboratively translate the Bible for different ethnic groups
After translations were completed and rigorously reviewed, they were sent for printing
In the early days, many of the beautiful prints were done in Hong Kong and then shipped to Taiwan
The distribution of the Bible included support for various churches, bookstores, and the development of different distribution channels
After retiring from the United Bible Societies, established 'Taiwan International Missions'

During this period, launched various mission projects to meet different needs, including Japanese churches, senior universities, grandparent choirs, 'Good Friend Mission', and the International Evangelical Association
The 'Good Friend Mission, A Center for Youth & Youth to be' continues to be carried on by the second generation
His son, Albert S. Lai, wrote the Self-Preface material tied to Toward A Community of Hope

quotes.text: Pastor Pingtung Lai (賴炳烔) is my father, and he was a student of Dr. Barclay.

He attended Tainan Theological College and Seminary(TTCS) from 1932 to 1936. In the academic year of 1935-1936, which was his final year at the TTCS, he was elected as the president of the student council.
In the early 1970s, I attempted to engage in trade with the Communist Party and worked in advertising, translation, printing, and publishing in Los Angeles.

Wrote the foreword dated June 15, 2025

Described FPCLA as the first Taiwanese church in North America
Called the church to become a missional community, not merely a haven for immigrants
Emphasized the spiritual call amid cultural transition
Described the concept of a 'hopeful community' as a lived imagination rooted in biblical truth
Stated that the church should be a beacon of hope and a witness to the gospel in the larger society

Earlier site letters list her as 書記 / 會計 / 婦女事工 in prior years — same person, successive offices

quotes.text: In 1971, Dr. Albert S. Lai published Toward A Community Of Hope — A Mission to Formosan Community in Los Angeles, a work both theological and prophetic in nature.
He called the church to transcend being merely a haven for immigrants and instead become a missional community, a beacon of hope and a witness to the gospel in the larger society.
The idea of a 'hopeful community' carries rich theological weight. It is not a slogan born of optimism or human willpower, but a lived imagination rooted in biblical truth.
Dr. Yunching Yeh Davis, 葉芸青, NTPC Moderator

facts: Is a Taiwanese Presbyterian pastor
Served as Moderator of the 70th General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in Taiwan (PCT)
Born in the 1960s
Authored the PCT foreword for the 2025 republication of Toward A Community of Hope
The foreword was dated June 15, 2025
In the foreword, described experiencing the changes and progress of various cultural, political, and religious environments in Taiwanese society
Resonated with the author's meticulous documentation of historical aspects and incisive analysis
Felt a deep sense of responsibility and mission towards history
Discussed the effort towards localization, indigenization, and uniqueness
Fostering innovative dialogue amidst competition and interdependence
Presented the concept of 'internal integration and external harmony' along with practical suggestions
Described this as a profound insight and wisdom
Encouraged each other, firmly believing that under the blessings of our Lord Jesus Christ, we will continue to build a beautiful society together in love
With immense hope, we will move towards universality, resiliently moving forward
Called to witness in every era that we are a community moving towards hope

quotes.text: Rev. En Sheng Pan, 潘恩盛, Moderator of the 70th General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in Taiwan

I have been deeply moved by my readings. The various journeys and historical testimonies left by the author, Dr. Albert S. Lai, and the pioneers of faith, both in Taiwan and in the immigrant environment, are truly commendable and worthy of recommendation to the church and society at large.

Among the many dialogues on various issues, it is rare that the author presents the concept of 'internal integration and external harmony,' along with practical suggestions, which is indeed a profound insight and wisdom.

As Taiwanese Christians, we encourage each other, firmly believing that under the blessings of our Lord Jesus Christ, we will continue to build a beautiful society together in love, and with immense hope, we will move towards universality, resiliently moving forward.

facts: Is a Taiwanese American pastor
Is the inaugural Chair of the NTPC Historical Committee (2025)
Authored the Historical Committee foreword to the 2025 republication of Toward A Community of Hope
The foreword was written in June 2025
The NTPC Historical Committee was formally established in 2025
He was asked to serve as its inaugural chairperson — an honor imbued with both solemn responsibility and sacred calling
In the foreword, stated that the history of the Church is a testament to the grace of God
Described the dissertation as a rare and invaluable document
Offered a detailed and moving account of the founding of the first Presbyterian Church in Taiwan in Southern California
Stated that the dissertation stands today as a cornerstone resource for understanding the development of Taiwanese Presbyterian Churches in the United States
The NTPC Executive Committee has formally endorsed and supported the publication of this work
On June 9, 2022, during an initial visit to Albert Lai, he chanced upon a doctoral dissertation sealed in dust for over half a century
He recommended translating and publishing the dissertation
In early 2023, visited Rev. Pinghsi Liu at Tainan East Gate Barclay Memorial Church and Brother Hsin Yuan Li of the Memorial Church
After sharing the historical and contextual significance, they swiftly reached a consensus to embark on a translation and publication endeavor
After two years of anticipation and preparation, the appointed time arrived in 2025
The year 2025 marks the 55th anniversary of the founding of the first Taiwanese church in Los Angeles
This book shall be the first publication of the NTPC Historical Committee
He also sat on the 51st Houston panel

quotes.text: The publication of this book is entirely the result of God's unexpected grace and blessing.
On the afternoon of June 9, 2022, during an initial visit to our esteemed brother, Albert Lai, I chanced upon a doctoral dissertation, sealed in dust for over half a century.
In the year 1967, Albert graduated from Tainan Theological College and Seminary. The following year, he journeyed across the seas to pursue further studies at San Francisco Theological Seminary.
Dr. Chaolong Kao was in place by September 1971, assuming the role of organizing pastor at the Formosan Presbyterian Church in Los Angeles.
Rev. Ching Fang Chen, 陳清芳, The Chair of NTPC Historical Committee

In early 2023, I visited the Rev. Ping Hsi Liu at Tainan East Gate Barclay Memorial Church and Brother Hsin Yuan Li of the Memorial Church.
